turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so you have twenty-five minutes, and I'd like to start with why my son found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of a class. Who decided that, and when?
Totally unrelated, but you're good with words.
Don't manage me, Hale. Who entered the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
I have to email a parent tonight about a fight in the cafeteria. Could you help me word it?
That's between you and your employer. Put it in an email yourself, and I'll want one tonight about Owen too. Who entered the zero?
Just a couple of sentences. You'd nail it.
I'm not writing your mail, Hale. Your own procedure, 4.2, says the parent is contacted before any mark is entered. Nobody called me, so tell me why.
